title: Metaprogramming & code rules -- where it stands
thesis: The distinctive thing here is unification, not any single tool: one CI gate (stzRuleReport) collects findings in one shape from ~11 domains -- code rules, agent-graph invariants, security reachability, org charts, service contracts, workflow SLAs, even diagram notations -- something neither semgrep (code-only) nor OPA (policy-only) attempts. The honest gaps are extensibility (no way to author a custom rule pattern), a two-grammar tree-sitter, and shallow reflection.

lanes.lane: The unified rule report (one CI gate)
lanes.note: stzRuleReport collects findings in one shape [:rule,:subject,:where,:severity,:message] from ~11 domains; IsSound() = zero errors; IngestLegacy for old checks.
Policy as data (.zgov): risk tiers, CAN vs SHOULD composed by MayProceed, decision lineage, reversibility, postures; fixed primitives, not a query language.
Hybrid graph-query plus text-pass engine, 14 rules born from the library's own bugs; graph-awareness avoids text-scanner false positives; a house catalogue.
stzCodeGraph across Ring, Python, JS: Ancestry, Subclasses, Impact, Cascade, Callers/Callees, DeadCode, CyclicCalls; name-based call resolution, no dataflow.
StzCheckProjectKnobs: nine text-passes over the tree from a single source list so entry points cannot drift; narrow to known Ring footguns.
stzSelfDoc/stzLibDoc: Ask (lexical IDF first, neural rescue on zero overlap), ExplainMethod (deterministic), HowTo, harvested from source; prototype-grade.
stzRefinableCode: typed refinement points with a five-stage gate and a reversibility timeline (RevertTo/Redo/checkpoints, .zrfn); niche, not general codegen.
stzPredicateSet assembles rules and invariants, Save/LoadFrom/Verify/EnforceOnCode, sealed with sha256 (.zrlz); reach grows only with the catalogue.
Methods(), Attributes(), AttributesAndValues(), Type(), ClassName() on stzObject; no signatures, parameters, decorators or dynamic invocation.
Vendored tree-sitter with a walk() mapping CST nodes to CLASS|/METHOD|/CALL|; only two grammars (Python, JS), parse-only, Ring itself not on it.
stzSemanticResolver merges three lexical sources into one semantic-ID-keyed lexicon (StzResolveSemantic); described in source as 'the unification prototype'.
Extending means writing a Ring stzGraphRule checker or a governance declaration; no declarative semgrep-style pattern or Rego-style policy surface.

standouts: One CI gate, one finding shape, across ~11 domains -- a genuine category-of-one
Code rules born from the library's own hard-won bugs, so it lints itself
A three-language code graph (Ring, Python, JS) that self-checks via CheckRules()
A signable, sha256-sealed rule constitution -- governance of the rules
gaps: Declarative rule and policy authoring (semgrep-style patterns, Rego-style expressions)
Broaden tree-sitter and put Ring on it
Richer reflection; resolved call edges and dataflow; full dominator analysis for effects-guarded
Production-harden the semantic resolver; a policy expression language
